title: Risk Management, Emergency Preparedness, and Business Continuity

content.text: Risk management is a planned, step-by-step process. It identifies, assesses, controls and monitors possible threats to your school's ability to achieve its educational mission. This framework applies to all types of risk: academic, operational, financial, reputational, regulatory, health and safety, safeguarding, and natural disasters.

Risk identification is an ongoing process with input from many stakeholders. The Principal works with the Senior Leadership Team, GM/Foundation Representative, Yayasan, staff, and external advisors to look for new and growing risks.

items: Curriculum gaps that affect Cambridge exam results or national curriculum compliance
Assessment malpractice or irregularities

Not meeting the Cambridge requirements or accreditation standards that apply (e.g., CIS or WASC)
Low enrollment or students leaving, which puts the program's future at risk
Digital divide (unequal access to devices and internet) that limits access to online learning

content.text: After a risk is identified, the school must assess its likelihood and its possible impact. This assessment sets the risk's priority. It also guides the plans to reduce the risk.
Use the 5×5 matrix below to rate each identified risk. Likelihood Scale:

steps: Rare: May happen only in unusual circumstances (<10% chance in 5 years)
Unlikely: Could occur at some time (10-30% chance in 5 years)
Possible: Might occur at some time (30-60% chance in 5 years)
Likely: Will probably happen (60-85% chance in 5 years)
Almost Certain: Expected to occur (>85% chance in 5 years)
content.title: Risk Assessment Matrix

steps: Insignificant: No significant impact on operations or reputation; minor first aid only
Minor: Short-term disruption that existing resources can manage; temporary negative attention
Moderate: Medium-term disruption that needs outside support; notable negative attention; injuries that need medical treatment
Major: Long-term disruption; significant stakeholder concern; hospitalization required; regulatory intervention
Catastrophic: Permanent disruption; potential school closure; fatality or permanent disability; criminal prosecution
content.title: Impact Scale:

content.text: Risk Rating = Likelihood × Impact
Risk Assessment Steps
Identify the Risk Describe the risk event clearly and the different ways it could happen
Example: "Earthquake during school hours causing structural damage and injuries"
Assess Likelihood Look at past data, expert advice and local conditions
Example: Set likelihood from the school's local hazard profile and official risk information (e.g., BNPB/BPBD/BMKG); do not use a network-wide default.
Assess Potential Impact Think about the worst case in each area: safety, learning, operations, reputation
Example: Major earthquake could cause "Major" to "Catastrophic" impact (rating: 4-5)

items: Calculate Initial Risk Score Multiply likelihood × impact

content.text: Example: 3 × 4 = 12 (High risk requiring immediate mitigation)

items: Identify Existing Controls Record the measures already in place that reduce likelihood or impact

content.text: Example: Earthquake-resistant building design, emergency response plan, regular drills

items: Assess Residual Risk Rate likelihood and impact again, taking existing controls into account
Determine Extra Mitigation If the residual risk is not acceptable, identify the further controls needed
content.title: Example: With controls, impact might reduce to "Moderate" (3), giving residual risk of 3 × 3 = 9 (Medium)

content.text: Example: Strengthen evacuation procedures, improve emergency supplies, increase drill frequency

The school risk register is a living document. It records all identified risks, their assessments, control measures, owners and monitoring schedules. The register should be kept in EduNav where the relevant module is available. Until then, schools must use a school-approved digital or paper risk register and update it regularly.
For each identified risk, document:

items: Risk ID: Unique identifier (e.g., ACA-001, OPS-023, SAF-015)
Risk Category: From categories above
Risk Description: Clear statement of the risk event and its possible consequences
Date Identified: When the risk was first added to the register
Risk Owner: Person responsible for monitoring and managing the risk (usually a member of the Senior Leadership Team, SLT)
Likelihood (Initial): Rating 1-5 before controls
Impact (Initial): Rating 1-5 before controls
Initial Risk Score: Likelihood × Impact
Current Controls: Measures already in place to prevent or reduce the risk
Likelihood (Residual): Rating 1-5 with current controls
Impact (Residual): Rating 1-5 with current controls
Residual Risk Score: Likelihood × Impact after controls
Risk Status: Target (acceptable), Tolerate (accept for now), Treat (mitigation planned), Transfer (insurance/contract), Terminate (eliminate activity)
Mitigation Actions: Extra measures needed to reduce residual risk
Action Owner: Person responsible for carrying out the mitigation
Target Completion: Deadline for mitigation actions
Monitoring Frequency: How often the risk is reviewed (monthly, quarterly, annually)
Last Reviewed: Date of most recent review
Next Review: Date of next scheduled review
Notes/Updates: Ongoing log of changes, incidents, or other useful information

Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk the school is willing to accept to achieve its educational mission. Different stakeholders may have different risk appetites:

items: Yayasan: Generally avoids risk on financial sustainability, legal compliance, and reputation
Eduversal Central: Low tolerance for risks that affect QMS standards, exam integrity, or accreditation
GM/Foundation Representative: Balanced approach that weighs educational innovation against operational stability
Principal: Must balance excellence and innovation with safety and compliance

1. Identify → 2. Assess → 3. Control → 4. Monitor → 5. Review → 1. Identify (repeat)

content.text: Risk management aims to prevent crises. Emergency response planning prepares the school to act well when incidents still happen despite prevention. This section sets out the structures, procedures, and protocols for responding to emergencies that threaten safety, disrupt operations, or need immediate action.
Not all incidents need the same level of response. The school uses a four-level classification system so that its action is proportionate and effective.
Definition: Local event with minimal impact that normal operations can manage
Examples:

items: Minor student injury (scraped knee, small cut)
Small classroom spill of non-hazardous materials
Brief power outage with backup systems functioning
Minor student behavioral incident
content.title: Level 1: Minor Incident

items: Handled by classroom teacher or immediate supervisor
Standard first aid or maintenance response
Incident logged in EduNav where available, or in the approved interim incident log
Parent notification if student injury
No need to activate emergency response team
content.title: Response:

content.text: Definition: Event that needs a coordinated response but does not threaten life or major operations
Examples:

items: Student injury that needs medical attention beyond first aid
Localized fire contained by fire extinguisher
Hazardous materials spill that needs the cleanup protocol
Serious student behavioral incident (fight, property damage)
Long utility failure affecting several areas
Security concern (suspicious person on campus)
content.title: Level 2: Significant Incident

items: Notify Principal or Vice Principal immediately
Activate relevant response protocols (fire, medical, security)
Contain incident and secure area
Record full details in EduNav where available, or in the approved interim incident log
Parent communication as appropriate
Incident review within 24 hours
Update the risk register if a pattern appears
content.title: Response:

content.text: Definition: Serious event that could affect multiple people or operations and needs a full emergency response
Examples:

items: Earthquake, fire, or flood affecting large parts of campus
Serious injury or medical emergency (heart attack, severe allergic reaction, major trauma)
Intruder on campus or security lockdown
Gas leak or other hazardous materials emergency
Missing student (especially from boarding facility)
Major transportation accident involving school vehicles
Violent incident or threat
content.title: Level 3: Major Emergency

items: Immediate: Principal (or most senior leader on site) takes the Incident Commander role
Activate Emergency Response Team
Contact emergency services (police, fire, ambulance) as needed
Start the relevant emergency protocol (evacuation, lockdown, shelter-in-place)
Account for all students and staff
Notify GM/Foundation Representative
Activate crisis communications plan
Parent notifications as soon as safely possible
Secure scene and preserve evidence if needed
Document everything
Post-incident debrief and report to Yayasan within 48 hours
content.title: Response:

content.text: Definition: A catastrophic (very serious) event that threatens life, needs outside emergency services and could attract media attention
Examples:

items: Fatality or multiple serious injuries
Major natural disaster (severe earthquake, tsunami warning)
Fire requiring evacuation of entire campus
Terrorist attack or armed threat
Serious crime (assault, sexual offense)
Major structural collapse
Epidemic outbreak requiring school closure
Multiple missing students
Any incident likely to attract media attention
content.title: Level 4: Critical Crisis

items: Immediate: Principal activates full Crisis Management Protocol

Call emergency services immediately. Use the school's verified local emergency contact plan. Use 112 where the local integrated 112 service is working. Police 110 is available across the whole country.
Emergency Response Team and Crisis Communication Team called in at full strength
Notify the GM/Foundation Representative, Yayasan leadership and Eduversal Central immediately
Carry out the emergency action plan (evacuation, lockdown, or shelter-in-place)
Establish command center and communication hub
Account for all students and staff; keep monitoring safety
Activate parent communication tree
Coordinate with emergency services and authorities
Name a media liaison (usually the GM/Foundation Representative or a designated spokesperson)
Arrange psychological first aid and counseling
Start the business continuity plan if operations are disrupted
Send daily situation reports to Yayasan and Eduversal Central
Full post-crisis review and formal investigation

content.text: The Emergency Response Team (ERT) is a group of staff members chosen in advance and trained to coordinate the school's response to emergencies. The team structure gives everyone clear roles. This helps the team act well even if some members are not available.
Incident Commander (Primary: Principal | Backup: Vice Principal/Senior SLT member) Responsibilities:

items: Take overall command and control of the emergency response
Assess situation and declare emergency level
Activate appropriate emergency protocols
Authorize evacuation, lockdown, or other protective actions
Coordinate with external emergency services
Make critical decisions about student/staff safety
Authorize communications to parents and external parties
Make sure all students and staff are accounted for
Declare "all clear" when emergency has passed

subsections.title: Emergency Types and Specific Response Protocols

content.text: Each type of emergency needs specific actions that fit its own features. The following protocols give detailed guidance for the most common emergency scenarios in Indonesian schools.
Immediate Actions:

steps.text: Discovery: Any person discovering fire immediately:
items: Activates nearest fire alarm pull station
Calls the locally verified fire/emergency service immediately. Use 112 where the local integrated 112 service is working. Schools must also keep the current local Damkar (fire service) number.
Only tries to put out the fire if it is small and safe to do so. Uses the PASS technique (Pull pin, Aim at base, Squeeze handle, Sweep side to side)

steps.text: Alarm Activation: When fire alarm sounds:
items: All staff: Stop all activities immediately
Teachers: Direct students to evacuate immediately and calmly by the designated route. Form an orderly line only when this does not delay evacuation.
Specialized areas: Lab, workshop, clinic, and kitchen staff secure or isolate hazardous materials only when this is immediately safe and does not delay evacuation
Follow designated evacuation routes (posted in each room)
Use secondary routes if primary route is blocked by smoke or fire
Close doors behind you if possible; do not delay evacuation to close windows or collect belongings
Feel doors before opening; use alternative route if door is hot
Stay low if smoke present (clean air near floor)
Do not use elevators under any circumstances
Help students with disabilities (using the buddy system set up in advance)
Go to the designated assembly points (away from buildings)
Teachers conduct roll call using class lists
Report missing persons immediately to Evacuation Coordinator
Stay at the assembly point until the "all clear" from the Incident Commander
Incident Commander meets fire brigade at gate
Provide building plans and information about missing persons
Identify hazards (gas lines, chemical storage)
Keep students and non-essential personnel away from the operational area (where emergency services are working)
Re-entry is allowed only after an all-clear from the competent emergency service/authority or, for a minor incident, the Incident Commander acting on a competent safety assessment
If you suspect fire, structural, electrical, gas or other damage, get a suitable safety assessment before letting people use the building again
Check for structural damage, smoke damage, water damage
Document damage thoroughly
Boarding Schools: A night-time fire alarm starts the residential staff response. Students evacuate in sleepwear if necessary. Blankets and emergency supplies are at the assembly points.
Science Labs: Never return to lab to retrieve experiments or materials
Special Needs: Evacuation assistants are assigned in advance to students with mobility issues. Visual/auditory alarms are provided for deaf/blind students.

Islamic Boarding Schools: Emergency modesty coverings or blankets may be stored near dorm exits or at assembly points. Evacuation must never be delayed to get a hijab, clothing, or other belongings. Gender-sensitive grouping may be used where appropriate. But safety, supervision, accessibility and accountability come first.
content.title: Special Considerations:

content.text: During Earthquake (Drop-Cover-Hold On):

items: Drop: Get down on hands and knees immediately (this stops you being knocked over)
Cover: Get under a sturdy desk, table, or against an interior wall; cover head and neck with arms
Hold On: Hold onto furniture/cover until shaking stops; be prepared for furniture to move
Classroom: Under desk, away from windows
Hallway: Against interior wall in duck-cover position
Playground/Outdoor: Move away from buildings, trees, utility poles; drop to ground
Cafeteria: Under tables if possible; away from kitchen with falling hazards
Science Lab: Away from glass, chemicals, equipment; under benches if possible
Mosque/Prayer Hall: Away from chandeliers, structural pillars; cover head
Vehicles: Stop safely; stay inside vehicle; avoid overpasses, power lines, trees
Do not run outside during shaking (falling debris danger)
Do not use doorways (it is a myth that doorways are stronger in modern buildings)
Do not use elevators
Do not go near windows or glass
When shaking stops, teachers and staff check the immediate route for obvious hazards. When the route is safe, teachers and staff begin a controlled evacuation to the designated open assembly area.
Do not delay evacuation for a detailed building inspection. Avoid areas with visible structural damage, gas leaks, fire, fallen glass, or electrical hazards.
Shelter-in-place is used only when evacuation would create a greater immediate danger, the route or assembly area is unsafe, or competent authorities instruct the school to remain inside.
Follow the school's posted earthquake evacuation route. Use stairs and do not use elevators. Move calmly to the designated assembly area.
Watch for aftershocks; be ready to drop-cover-hold on again
Avoid damaged areas of campus
Assembly points should be in open areas away from buildings and overhead hazards
While the evacuation route or outside area is unsafe, stay in the safest available area. Keep away from windows, glass, external walls and falling hazards.
Move away from windows and external walls
Conduct roll call in place
Prepare for possible evacuation if aftershock causes damage
Structural cracks or damage
Gas leaks (smell, listen for hissing)
Electrical hazards (sparks, exposed wires)
Water line breaks
Chemical spills
Fire hazards
Mark unsafe areas clearly; restrict access
Parent notification: The school is safe, students are accounted for, and more updates will follow
Update every 30-60 minutes until situation stable
Coordinate pickup procedures if early dismissal needed
Expect aftershocks; they may come hours or days later
Each aftershock: Drop-Cover-Hold On
Monitor Indonesian geophysical agency (BMKG) for updates
Night-time earthquakes: Students Drop-Cover-Hold On during shaking. When shaking stops and the route is safe, residential staff lead a controlled evacuation to the designated open assembly area.
Residential staff take the dorm register/emergency roster and do a roll call at the assembly area. Do not delay evacuation to search rooms when conditions are unsafe.
If the evacuation route or outdoor assembly area is unsafe, use the temporary safe area chosen in advance. Wait there for further instructions from the Incident Commander or local authorities.
Counseling support for traumatized students
Accommodation arrangements if buildings unsafe
content.title: Boarding School Earthquake Considerations:

content.text: Flooding can come from heavy rain (common in many parts of Indonesia), drainage failures, coastal/tidal effects, or a nearby river overflowing. Pre-Flood Preparation (Monsoon Season Readiness):

steps: Monitor weather forecasts and flood warnings from BMKG
Inspect drainage systems; clear debris
Position sandbags at vulnerable entry points
Raise critical equipment (servers, electrical panels) to a higher level
Prepare emergency supplies on upper floors
Review evacuation routes to higher ground
content.title: Flooding Emergency

steps.text: Early Warning: If there is a flash flood warning or heavy rain:
items: Move students to upper floors early, before flooding starts
Shut down electrical systems in lower levels
Secure valuable equipment and documents
Activate flood response plan
If water enters buildings: Evacuate to upper floors immediately
Do not try to walk through moving water (15cm can knock an adult off their feet)
Avoid electrocution: Turn off power; assume standing water carries electricity
Close doors/windows to slow water entry
Account for all students and staff on safe floors
If evacuation is impossible: Shelter on the highest floors
Call the locally verified emergency service (use 112 where the local integrated service is working). Report your location, the number of people and the conditions.
Prepare rooftop access for helicopter rescue if necessary
Use emergency supplies sparingly; save phone battery power
Only if there is a life-threatening emergency (fire, structural collapse)
Link arms or hold ropes to stay together
Test depth with stick; avoid fast-moving water
Watch for hidden hazards (open manholes, debris, animals)

steps: Do Not Return Until Authorized: Incident Commander assesses safety

items: Structural damage from water pressure
Contaminated water (sewage, chemicals, disease)
Electrical hazards
Mold and health hazards
Slippery surfaces
Professional cleaning company for sewage-contaminated areas
Document damage for insurance
Dispose of contaminated food, materials
Dry and disinfect thoroughly

steps: Health Monitoring: Watch for diseases spread by water; encourage handwashing; avoid contact with floodwater
content.title: Post-Flood Response:

content.text: Priority: Preserve Life → Prevent Deterioration → Promote Recovery
Immediate Response:

steps: Assess Scene Safety: Make sure the area is safe for responders

items: Airway: Is airway open?
Breathing: Is person breathing adequately?
Circulation: Is there pulse/severe bleeding?
Disability: Level of consciousness? Spinal injury suspected?
Call the school's locally verified ambulance/medical emergency service; use 112 where the local integrated 112 service is working
School clinic/First Aid Officer
Notify Principal immediately

content.title: Medical Emergency (Serious Injury or Illness)

items: Cardiac Arrest: Start CPR immediately; use the AED (automated external defibrillator)
Severe Bleeding: Press directly on the wound; raise the wound; use pressure points if needed; use a tourniquet only as a last resort
Choking: Abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) if the person is conscious; CPR if unconscious
Give the EpiPen if available and prescribed to the student
Call ambulance immediately
Position: lying down with legs raised, unless the student has difficulty breathing (then sitting)
Monitor and be ready to perform CPR
A second dose of epinephrine may be given after 5-15 minutes if there is no improvement
Poisoning: Call poison control; do not make the person vomit unless you are specifically told to
Severe Burns: Cool the burn with running water for 20 minutes; cover with a clean cloth; treat for shock
Spinal Injury Suspected: Do not move the person unless they are in immediate danger; keep the head and neck still
content.title: Life-Threatening Emergencies (Act Immediately):

items: Fractures: Keep the injured part still; apply ice; raise it if possible; medical evaluation needed
Head Injury with Loss of Consciousness: Do not move the person; monitor breathing and consciousness; medical evaluation required
Protect from injury (move dangerous objects away)
Put something soft under the head; turn the student on their side if possible
Time the seizure. If it lasts longer than 5 minutes, or there are multiple seizures, call an ambulance.
Do not restrain or put anything in mouth
Stay with student until fully conscious; position on side during recovery
Help student use inhaler (puff + spacer if available)
Sit upright; stay calm
If there is no improvement after 10-15 minutes, or symptoms get worse, call an ambulance
Hypoglycemia (low blood sugar): Give fast-acting sugar (juice, candy) if the student is conscious
Hyperglycemia (high blood sugar): Needs medical treatment; call an ambulance if symptoms are severe

content.title: Serious But Not Immediately Life-Threatening:

items: Time of incident and discovery
Student name, age, class
Symptoms and assessment findings
Actions taken (first aid, medications given, etc.)
Time ambulance called and arrived
Hospital transported to
Staff members involved
Parent notification time and response
content.title: Medical Emergency Documentation:

items: Immediate call to parents for any emergency that needs ambulance transport
Provide factual information: what happened, injuries/symptoms, actions taken, current status
Hospital information and how parents can proceed
A staff member goes with the student to hospital if a parent cannot arrive immediately
content.title: Parent Communication:

items: Incident report completed within 24 hours
Parent meeting to discuss incident and any ongoing care needs
Medical clearance before returning to school if the student was hospitalized
Care plan for students with ongoing medical needs
Staff debrief if traumatic incident
content.title: Follow-Up:

content.text: Threat Assessment:

items: Low Threat: Unauthorized person on campus but no indication of harmful intent
Medium Threat: Suspicious behavior, verbal threats, person appears agitated or unstable
High Threat: Weapon visible, active violence, credible threat of harm
content.title: Security Threat or Intruder

steps: Security or staff approach person calmly
Ask the purpose of the visit; escort the person to visitor check-in
If cooperative: Complete visitor procedures
If uncooperative: Ask to leave; call security backup
Notify Principal if person refuses to leave
Call police if trespassing continues
content.title: Low Threat Response:

steps: Do not approach; maintain distance
Call security and Principal immediately
Describe person, location, behavior

items: Classes continue but doors locked
No outdoor activities; students remain in buildings
No campus movement unless essential
Heightened awareness

steps: Security assesses situation; calls police if needed
Notify GM/Foundation Representative
Keep the soft lockdown until the threat is resolved
Parent notification if extended
content.title: Medium Threat Response:

steps: Immediate Alert: "LOCKDOWN LOCKDOWN LOCKDOWN" over PA system or emergency notification

items: Move inside nearest secure room immediately
Lock doors; barricade with furniture if possible
Close windows and blinds
Turn off lights
Silence phones (silent mode, not vibrate)
Move away from doors and windows; hide if possible
Sit on floor in silence
Do not open the door for anyone until a verified authority gives the "all clear"
Move away from buildings toward exit or safe area
Run in zig-zag pattern if necessary
Do not gather in large groups
Leave campus if it is safe to do so; find a secure location
Evacuate building if safe exit available
Hide in inaccessible location (locked closet, etc.)
As absolute last resort: Prepare to defend or flee if confronted

content.title: High Threat Response - Full Lockdown:

items: Incident Commander coordinates with police
Remain in lockdown until police give "all clear"
Cooperate fully with police; provide information
Police will clear building room by room; follow instructions exactly
content.title: Law Enforcement Arrival:

items: Comprehensive security review
Counseling for affected students and staff
Family meetings
Communication plan for community
Potential media management
Long-term security improvements
content.title: Post-Incident:

items: Residential buildings included in lockdown
Security patrol of dormitories
24/7 security presence
Communication with parents may be delayed if the incident happens at night; update parents as soon as it is safe to do so
content.title: Boarding School Considerations:

content.text: Internal Chemical Spill (Science Lab):

items: Evacuate the lab immediately if there are vapors, a large spill, or an unknown substance
Close door; post warning sign
Alert lab technician and Principal
Activate chemical spill response team if available
Trained staff use spill kit to contain and neutralize
Ventilate area
Dispose of contaminated materials according to regulations
Document incident
Evacuate building or area
Call fire brigade (hazmat team)
Provide SDS (Safety Data Sheet) to responders
Account for all persons
Medical evaluation for anyone exposed
Evacuate the building immediately (do not activate the fire alarm, because of the risk of an electrical spark)
No smoking, flames, or sparks
Do not use electrical switches, phones, or electronics
Call the gas company emergency line and the fire brigade from a safe location
Open windows if safe to do so
Shut off gas supply at meter if accessible and safe

steps: Do Not Re-Enter: Wait until the gas company declares it safe
content.title: Gas Leak:

items: Close all windows and doors
Turn off HVAC (air conditioning and ventilation) to stop outside air coming in
Seal gaps with wet towels if possible
Move to interior rooms away from windows
Monitor radio/news for updates from authorities
Do not evacuate unless authorities instruct you to (risk of exposure)
Follow designated evacuation routes away from hazard
Transport arrangements for students if needed

content.title: External Hazmat Incident (e.g., industrial accident nearby):

steps: TSUNAMI - natural warning signs. A strong or long earthquake near the coast, a sudden rise or fall in sea level, or a loud roar from the sea are themselves the warning. Do NOT wait for an official alert.

TSUNAMI - immediate action. At a coastal school, once shaking stops, evacuate inland or to high ground immediately, preferably on foot. Do not wait for an official alert. If no high ground is reachable, move to the designated vertical-evacuation location or the highest safe level of a suitable strong building. Follow the school's local tsunami plan.

TSUNAMI - this overrides the standard post-earthquake process. At a coastal school, tsunami evacuation takes priority once shaking stops. Move inland or to high ground immediately. Do not wait for a building assessment or an official alert.
TSUNAMI - all-clear. Return only when BMKG (Badan Meteorologi, Klimatologi, dan Geofisika) or the local BPBD issues an official all-clear. A receding first wave does not mean the event is over.
VOLCANIC - alert monitoring. Track PVMBG alert levels (Level I Normal, II Waspada, III Siaga, IV Awas) for any volcano within range of the school.
content.title: Tsunami and Volcanic Eruption Protocols

content.text: At Level III, review the evacuation plan with staff; at Level IV, follow BPBD instructions immediately.

steps: VOLCANIC - ashfall. Shelter in place. Close all windows and doors, shut down HVAC and air intakes, and distribute N95 masks and eye protection. Keep students indoors until ashfall stops.

VOLCANIC - roof load. Volcanic ash is heavy, especially when wet. Watch how much ash builds up on roofs. Evacuate any building where the load becomes a structural concern. Clear roofs only when it is safe to do so.

BOTH - schools in exposed districts. Any school in a coastal or volcanic-risk district adds the relevant drill or exercise to its annual calendar. The school also identifies its evacuation route, safe destination, and assembly/accountability arrangements in advance. It does this in coordination with local BPBD/authorities where available.

content.text: Good evacuation depends on clear procedures that are practiced regularly in drills.
Evacuate When:

items: Fire alarm activation (automatic evacuation)
Earthquake: after shaking stops, conduct controlled evacuation to the designated safe assembly area unless the route or outdoor area is unsafe or authorities instruct otherwise
Gas leak or hazmat incident
Bomb threat (after assessment)
Flood water entering buildings
Any situation where building occupancy is unsafe
content.title: Evacuation Decision-Making

items: External hazmat incident with airborne contaminants
Severe weather (extreme lightning, destructive winds, or other conditions making outdoor movement unsafe)
External security threat (safer inside)
Earthquake only when the evacuation route or outdoor assembly area is more hazardous than the current protected location, or competent authorities instruct shelter-in-place
content.title: Do Not Evacuate (Shelter-in-Place) When:

content.text: Teachers/Staff in Classrooms:

steps: Immediately direct students to line up at door
Take class register/roll book
Quickly look around the whole room (check restrooms, under desks)
Close windows and doors (but do not lock)
Turn off lights if time permits
Lead class via designated route to assembly point
Keep students together as one group
Take roll call at the assembly point
Report status (all present / missing students) to Evacuation Coordinator
Supervise students until "all clear" or further instructions
content.title: Evacuation Roles and Responsibilities

steps: Hear alarm; begin floor/area sweep
Check all rooms (classrooms, restrooms, offices, closets)
Direct any remaining occupants to evacuate
Check stairwells are clear
Close fire doors if applicable
Be last to leave floor/building
Report to Incident Commander: "Floor/Building [X] clear" or report issues
content.title: Floor/Building Wardens (designated staff for each building/floor):

steps: Shut down gas lines if safe to do so
Make sure fire exits and routes are accessible
Assist with evacuating persons with disabilities if needed
Bring building plans to Incident Commander
Stand by to support emergency services
content.title: Facilities/Maintenance Staff:

steps: Control campus access; prevent entry during evacuation
Direct traffic flow away from buildings
Keep evacuation routes clear
Assist with crowd control at assembly points
Coordinate with external emergency responders
content.title: Security Staff:

steps: Bring emergency communication devices (phones, megaphone)
Bring emergency contact lists
Support Communication Officer with parent notifications
Bring emergency supplies to assembly point if time permits
content.title: Administrative/Support Staff:

content.text: Assembly points are open areas, chosen in advance, at a safe distance from buildings. Primary Assembly Points:

items: Early Years/Primary: Front field area away from buildings
Secondary: Main sports field or designated open area
Boarding Students: Separate assembly area near residential buildings
Staff Only: Designated section of assembly area
content.title: Assembly Points

items: At the distance set by the site's hazard assessment. Use at least 50 meters where practical. Go farther where collapse, glass, fire, power-line, tsunami, or other hazards require it
Away from overhead hazards (trees, power lines)
Avoid areas near gas lines or underground utilities
Accessible from multiple evacuation routes
Clear sight lines for supervision
Enough space for the whole school population, standing in class groups
Accessible surface (not muddy or uneven)
Shaded if possible (tropical heat considerations)
content.title: Criteria for Assembly Points:

items: Alternative open areas on campus
Off-campus locations (e.g., nearby park, mosque, community center)
Arranged in advance through MOUs (Memoranda of Understanding) with neighboring properties
content.title: Secondary Assembly Points (use if primary blocked or unsafe):

items: Class flags or signs for easy student grouping
First aid supplies
Emergency contact lists
Communication devices
Water and basic supplies in case of an extended evacuation
Shade structures if available
content.title: Assembly Point Equipment:

content.text: Early Years (Ages 3-5):

items: Hold hands with buddy; teacher leads, assistant at rear
Use simple evacuation song or chant to keep calm and together
Extra attention to making sure every student is accounted for
Comfort items (favorite toy, blanket) are acceptable if time permits
Parents may need to pick up children immediately; controlled process for reuniting children with parents
content.title: Evacuation Procedures by School Section

items: Line up quickly and quietly; walk briskly but do not run
Buddy system (accountability partners)
Older students may assist younger
The teacher tells students the reason for the evacuation if this is age-appropriate
content.title: Primary (Ages 5-11):

items: Students expected to be more independent; move quickly and responsibly
Students may need to evacuate from subject classrooms with teachers who are not their homeroom teacher
Roll call by the subject class teacher at the assembly point; checked against homeroom lists
Older students may be assigned specific roles (assisting younger students, carrying supplies)
content.title: Secondary (Ages 11-18):

items: Nighttime evacuations: Emergency lighting; clear signage
Students evacuate in nightwear if necessary; blankets at assembly point
Residential staff conduct roll call by dormitory
Separate male/female assembly areas if culturally appropriate
content.title: Boarding Students:

items: Individualized evacuation plans for students with mobility, sensory, or cognitive challenges
Assigned evacuation assistants (buddy + staff)
Special equipment if needed (evacuation chair for multi-story buildings)
Visual and auditory alarms for deaf/hard of hearing students
Simple, direct language for students with cognitive disabilities
Extra support for students with anxiety disorders (familiar adult, comfort objects)
content.title: Students with Special Needs:

content.text: Roll Call Procedures:

steps: Class Teachers: Take roll call immediately on arrival at the assembly point, using the class register

items: "Class [X] all present"
"Class [Y] missing [number] students: [names]"

steps: Specialist Teachers: Report the status of students who were in their classes when the alarm sounded
Administrative Check: Compare the reports to make sure there are no duplicates or gaps
Staff Roll Call: Administrative staff account for all adult staff members
content.title: Accounting for All Students and Staff

steps: Evacuation Coordinator immediately informs Incident Commander of missing persons
Verification: Confirm missing person was on campus (check attendance records, sign-in logs)

steps.text: If Confirmed On Campus and Missing:
items: Notify emergency services immediately
Provide name, age, last known location, description, photo if available
Floor/Building Wardens conduct secondary search if safe to do so
Parents of missing student(s) notified immediately

steps: If Person Located: Report immediately to Incident Commander and Evacuation Coordinator; update emergency services
content.title: Missing Persons Protocol:

content.text: "All Clear" Declaration: Only the Incident Commander can authorize the return
Inspection Before Re-entry:

items: Facilities team inspects for structural damage, hazards, contamination
Emergency services give clearance if they responded
Utilities functional and safe (power, gas, water)
Environment safe (air quality, temperature, no smoke/fumes)
content.title: Controlled Return to Buildings

steps: Small inspection team enters first
If safe, staff enter to prepare classrooms
Students return by section or class group (this avoids crowding)
Resume normal operations or adjust schedule as needed
content.title: Phased Return:

items: Activate business continuity plan (see Section 15.3)
Arrange alternative location or early dismissal
Communication with parents about pickup or other arrangements
content.title: If Buildings Not Safe:

content.text: Good communication in an emergency needs clear roles, messages planned in advance, and stakeholder groups in order of priority.

steps: Speed: Communicate as soon as it is safe to do so; even "we are aware and assessing" is useful
Accuracy: Only share confirmed facts; do not guess
Consistency: All spokespersons use the same information; no contradictions
Transparency: Share what you know and what you don't know; don't hide bad news
Empathy: Acknowledge fear, concern, and impact on community
Action-Oriented: Tell stakeholders what you are doing and what they should do
Continuity: Update regularly even if there is no new information; silence creates rumors
content.title: Communication Principles During Crisis

content.text: Crisis Communication Team
Incident Commander: Authorizes all communications; approves messages
Communication Officer: Drafts and sends communications
GM/Foundation Representative: Primary spokesperson for media and external parties
Principal: May serve as spokesperson for internal community (parents, staff) depending on situation
Eduversal Central Communications: Supports with template messages, media relations, and coordination across partner schools
Immediate (within 30 minutes of incident):

items: Emergency Services: If called, provide situation report
On-Site Staff: Briefing on situation and required actions
GM/Foundation Representative: Immediate notification of Level 3 or 4 emergencies
Yayasan Leadership: For Level 3 or 4 emergencies
content.title: Stakeholder Communication Priority

items: Parents of Directly Affected Students: Individual calls for students injured, hospitalized, or directly involved
All Parents: General notification of incident, status of students, school actions
Eduversal Central: Formal incident report
All Staff Not On Site: Information about incident and expectations
content.title: Urgent (within 1-2 hours):

items: Yayasan Board: Formal briefing
Relevant Authorities: Indonesian education ministry, Cambridge (if exam-related), health authorities (if health incident)
Media: If there are inquiries or public interest; coordinated response only
content.title: Important (within 3-6 hours):

items: School Community: Detailed update on situation, next steps, support available
Partner Schools: The Eduversal network is informed if there are lessons learned or risks relevant to them
content.title: Follow-Up (within 24 hours):

content.text: For Parents:

items: Primary: SMS blast (fastest; highest open rate in Indonesia)
Secondary: Email with more details
Tertiary: WhatsApp groups (if established)
Phone Calls: For parents of directly affected students
School Website: Updated status page
Social Media: Brief status updates on school Facebook/Instagram
content.title: Communication Channels

items: Primary: SMS or WhatsApp to all staff
Secondary: Email for detailed information
Staff Meeting: Face-to-face briefing as soon as possible
content.title: For Staff:

items: Directly: Teachers brief students age-appropriately in classrooms once safe
Via Parents: For younger students or if the school closes
content.title: For Students:

items: Media: Designated spokesperson only; prepared statements; refer all inquiries to GM/Foundation Representative
Authorities: Principal or GM as required by regulations
content.title: For External Parties:

content.text: Template Communications
Initial Parent Notification - Incident Occurred

English: "Dear Parents, we are writing to tell you about an incident at [School Name] today involving [brief description]. All students and staff are safe and accounted for. We have [actions taken]. We will send an update within [timeframe]. Please do not come to school at this time, so that emergency personnel can work. We will tell you if early pickup is required. Thank you for your understanding."

Bahasa Indonesia: "Kepada Orang Tua/Wali yang terhormat, kami menginformasikan telah terjadi insiden di [Nama Sekolah] hari ini terkait [deskripsi singkat]. Seluruh siswa dan staf dalam kondisi aman dan telah dihitung keberadaannya. Kami telah [tindakan yang diambil]. Kami akan memberikan informasi lebih lanjut dalam [jangka waktu]. Mohon untuk tidak datang ke sekolah saat ini agar petugas darurat dapat bekerja. Kami akan memberitahu jika diperlukan penjemputan lebih awal. Terima kasih atas pengertiannya."
Update - Situation Resolved

English: "Update: The situation at [School Name] has been resolved. [Brief explanation of resolution]. Students have returned to class and school operations are continuing normally. No injuries occurred. We appreciate your patience. A full report will be shared [timeframe]."

Bahasa Indonesia: "Informasi terbaru: Situasi di [Nama Sekolah] telah teratasi. [Penjelasan singkat]. Siswa telah kembali ke kelas dan kegiatan sekolah berjalan normal. Tidak ada yang terluka. Kami menghargai kesabaran Anda. Laporan lengkap akan dibagikan [jangka waktu]."
Early Dismissal / School Closure Notification

English: "Dear Parents, because of [reason], school is ending early today at [time]. Please arrange to pick up your child at this time. Buses will run their routes early. Students will be supervised until they are picked up. Tomorrow's school schedule [will resume normally / is canceled / will be decided and communicated by 6 PM]. Thank you for your flexibility."

Bahasa Indonesia: "Kepada Orang Tua/Wali, dikarenakan [alasan], kami melakukan penutupan sekolah lebih awal hari ini pada pukul [waktu]. Mohon untuk menjemput anak Anda pada waktu tersebut. Bus akan beroperasi lebih awal. Siswa akan diawasi hingga dijemput. Jadwal sekolah besok [akan berjalan normal / dibatalkan / akan diputuskan dan dikomunikasikan pukul 18.00]. Terima kasih atas pengertiannya."
Crisis response depends on accurate emergency contact information that staff can access easily.
Information Required for Each Student:

items: Parent/guardian full names
Mobile phone numbers (primary and secondary)
Other emergency contacts (at least 2; not parents)
Home address
Work addresses and phone numbers
Email addresses
Preferred contact method and language
Medical information (allergies, conditions, medications)
Special instructions (custody arrangements, restraining orders)
content.title: Emergency Contact Database

items: Emergency contact person (relationship, phone number)
Secondary emergency contact
Medical information
Home address
content.title: Information Required for Each Staff Member:

items: Updated annually at enrollment/re-enrollment
Checked every term (parents confirm or update the details each term)

Stored in EduNav where available, or in a secure system the school has approved. Access is limited by role, and UU No. 27/2022 applies to how the information is handled. Collect, use, keep and share only the information needed for legitimate school and emergency-response purposes
Backup paper copies kept in the Principal's office and in the emergency response kit
Tested every year, with a parent notification linked to a drill
content.title: Data Management:

content.text: The school must keep a leader available 24/7 for escalated serious emergencies, through a written on-call arrangement. The Principal is the main lead. A clearly named backup leads when the Principal is not available. Communication Pathways:

items.text: Designated emergency contact number provided to:
items: GM/Foundation Representative
Vice Principal
Security Supervisor (for overnight/weekend emergencies)
Yayasan leadership
Eduversal Central emergency contacts
Backup: If the Principal is not available, the Vice Principal takes over the role with full authority

External emergency contact sheet: Keep a list of local emergency numbers and check it at least once a term. Include 112 (where it works), Police 110, Damkar (fire and rescue service), BPBD, the nearest Puskesmas/hospital/ambulance, utilities, and other emergency services relevant to your area. Consider a separate school emergency phone number for serious incidents.
content.title: 24/7 Leadership Escalation Coverage

items: The on-call leader acknowledges Level 3/4 alerts as soon as possible and starts the response chain immediately. The school sets a written response-time expectation and communicates it
If dealing with a personal matter: Confirm you received the alert and hand the immediate response to the Deputy/SLT (Senior Leadership Team) member
For Level 3 or 4 emergencies: start the emergency response chain immediately and take on or delegate the Incident Commander role
For Level 1 or 2: Give guidance; the on-call leader may not need to come to campus
content.title: Response Expectations:

items: Overnight residential staff have a direct line to the designated on-call leader
Boarding schools must make sure that a named senior leader/on-call decision-maker can be reached quickly overnight. Where this person physically stays is decided locally
Clear protocols that let residential staff handle nighttime incidents on their own if there is immediate risk before the Principal arrives
content.title: Boarding Schools - Enhanced Requirements:

content.text: Tier 1 (notify immediately):

items: GM/Foundation Representative (by Incident Commander directly)
Senior Leadership Team members
Emergency Response Team members
content.title: Emergency Contact Tree

items: Yayasan leadership (by GM/Foundation Representative)
Eduversal Central emergency contact (by GM/Foundation Representative)
All teaching staff (by Communication Officer)
Support staff heads
content.title: Tier 2 (notify within 30 minutes):

items: Parents of all students (by Communication Officer using mass notification system)
Staff not in Tier 2
content.title: Tier 3 (notify within 1 hour):

items: Relevant authorities (by Principal or GM as required)
Media/public (by GM/Foundation Representative if necessary)
content.title: Tier 4 (notify within 2-3 hours):

content.text: Lockdown and shelter-in-place are protective actions that keep students and staff inside buildings for safety.
Purpose: Secure buildings and rooms to keep out an intruder or dangerous person
When Used:

items: Intruder on campus with weapon or violent behavior
Threat of violence from outside the school
Hostage situation
Armed attacker or active violence (rare but included in preparedness planning)
Serious crime in progress on or near campus
content.title: Lockdown (Security Threat)

content.text: Types of Lockdown:

items: ALL doors locked immediately
ALL windows closed and covered
Lights off
Hide out of sight from doors/windows
Complete silence (phones on silent, no talking)
Do not open the door for anyone until a verified authority gives the "all clear"
Duration: Until police clear building or Incident Commander gives "all clear"
content.title: Full/Hard Lockdown (Imminent Threat):

items: Doors locked but classes continue
Students remain in classrooms
No one enters or exits buildings
No outdoor activities
No one moves around campus except essential staff with a radio or other communication device
Duration: Until the threat is assessed and resolved
content.title: Soft Lockdown (Precautionary):

items: PA System: "LOCKDOWN, LOCKDOWN, LOCKDOWN"
Alarm: A sound pattern that is different from the fire alarm
Radio/Phone: Security or Principal notifies staff
content.title: Lockdown Announcement:

content.text: Specific Lockdown Actions by Location:

steps: Lock door immediately (if no lock, barricade with furniture)
Close blinds/curtains
Move students away from doors and windows to the least visible area
Turn off lights; silence phones
Conduct silent roll call (headcount)
Keep students calm and quiet
Do not respond to knocks or calls unless the "all clear" is verified
content.title: In Classroom:

steps: Move to nearest classroom or secure room immediately
If no room can be reached, hide in a lockable bathroom stall, closet, or other space
Lock/barricade if possible
Silence phone; do not make noise
content.title: In Hallway/Bathroom:

steps: If exits can be reached, evacuate from campus immediately (run in a zig-zag; spread out)
If there is no safe exit, move to the most secure part of the space (storage room, kitchen)
Barricade doors with tables, equipment
Turn off lights; hide behind cover
Silence phones
content.title: In Cafeteria/Gym/Assembly Area:

steps: Evaluate: Can you safely evacuate campus? (Yes → RUN; No → HIDE)
If evacuating: Run away from threat; zig-zag pattern; seek safe location off campus
If you cannot evacuate: Hide in a place away from main pathways; stay low; silence your phone
content.title: Outside:

items: Announced by Incident Commander only
May include a set phrase or code word to show the message is genuine
Verified authority: Police or Principal in person at door
content.title: "All Clear" Signal:

items: Counseling available for students/staff experiencing distress
Parent communication explaining incident and school response
Debrief meeting with staff
Security review and improvements
content.title: Post-Lockdown Support:

content.text: Purpose: Keep students/staff inside so they are not exposed to a hazard outside
When Used:

items: Hazmat (hazardous materials) incident nearby (chemical spill, gas release, fire with toxic smoke)
Severe weather (tornado, extreme lightning, hailstorm)
Air quality emergency (volcanic ash, extreme pollution, smoke from wildfire)
An event outside that makes evacuation more dangerous than staying inside
content.title: Shelter-in-Place (Environmental Hazard)

items: Students and staff outdoors move inside immediately
Close and lock exterior doors
Close all windows and exterior doors
Turn off HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) systems so outside air does not come in
Seal gaps around doors/windows with wet towels or tape if there is a serious threat in the air
Interior rooms with no windows (or minimal)
Away from outside walls if there is a risk of explosion
Central hallways or interior classrooms
Teachers conduct roll call
Report any missing persons to Incident Commander
Incident Commander follows emergency broadcasts, updates from authorities, and the weather
Updates staff via radio or phone
Prepares to evacuate if the authorities order it
Continue classes or activities if possible
Provide updates to students age-appropriately
Keep students busy with learning activities and games
Authorities give clearance
Incident Commander announces "all clear"
Gradually resume normal operations
Battery-powered radio for emergency broadcasts
First aid kits
Water and non-perishable food
Duct tape and plastic sheeting (for sealing rooms if needed)
Flashlights and batteries
Student comfort items (books, games, blankets)
content.title: Shelter-in-Place Supplies:

content.text: Business continuity planning makes sure that learning and essential school operations can continue, or restart quickly, after a disruption. Emergency response focuses on immediate safety. Business continuity focuses on keeping operations running and on recovery.
Identify which functions are essential to the school's mission and what they depend on.

items: Dependencies: Staff, safe facilities, communication systems
Dependencies: Teachers, curriculum materials, learning spaces (physical or digital), student access
Dependencies: Exam materials, invigilators, secure storage, communication with Cambridge

content.text: Off-campus activities and educational trips add to learning, but they also bring extra risks. Thorough risk assessment and approval processes are essential.
Different activities require different levels of assessment and approval, based on their risk profile.
Category A: Low Risk - Local, Routine Activities
Examples: Walking field trip to nearby park/mosque/museum; local community service; guest speaker on campus; sports match at nearby school
Risk Profile: Low risk; supervised by school staff; familiar place; short (less than 4 hours)
Approval Required: The Subject Leader or Year Level Coordinator approves; the Principal is informed
Risk Assessment: Simplified checklist
Category B: Medium Risk - Extended Local or Regular Competitive Events
Examples: Full-day trip to Jakarta attraction; inter-school sports tournament; overnight camping within province; educational tour to historical site
Risk Profile: Moderate risk; needs transportation; full day or overnight; physical activity; larger group
Approval Required: The Principal approves in writing; the GM/Foundation Representative is informed
Risk Assessment: Standard risk assessment form
Category C: High Risk - Adventure, Specialized, or International
Examples: Mountain climbing, water sports, ropes course; international educational trip; Olympiad competition requiring air travel; outdoor education camp with challenging activities
Risk Profile: Higher risk; specialized activities; expert supervision required; international travel; high cost; long duration
Approval Required: The Principal and the GM/Foundation Representative both approve; the Yayasan is informed
Risk Assessment: Full risk assessment; site visit recommended; checks on (vetting of) external providers
Every off-campus activity requires a written risk assessment. The trip leader completes it, and the Principal approves it.

content.text: Format: A 2-3 hour guided discussion based on a scenario
Example Scenarios:

Scenario 1: Major Earthquake. A 7.0 magnitude earthquake hits during school hours. The science building has structural damage. There are multiple injuries, and communications are disrupted. Aftershocks are expected. Parents are rushing to school. Roads are blocked. Discussion:

items: How do we assess building safety? Who decides whether to evacuate or shelter?
How do you look after injured people when ambulances are delayed?
How communicate if internet/phone down?
What are the priorities in the first hour? In the first 24 hours?
If the campus is unusable, where do you move to? How does learning continue?
How support traumatized students/staff?

content.text: Scenario 2: Serious Student Injury on International Trip. A student falls at a climbing facility in Singapore and is seriously injured. The student is taken to hospital. The parents are in Indonesia. Police are investigating. Discussion:

items: Trip leader's immediate priority?
How communicate with parents?
Who travels to Singapore to give support?
Legal and insurance considerations?
How do you manage the rest of the group (continue or return)?
What documentation needed?
Support classmates who witnessed?

content.text: Scenario 3: Safeguarding Allegation Against Staff. A student tells a teacher that another staff member made inappropriate physical contact. The disclosure is credible and detailed. Discussion:

items: Immediate steps upon disclosure?
How ensure student safety?
Actions regarding staff member?
Who do you notify (authorities, Yayasan, Eduversal, parents)?
Balance confidentiality with safety?
What support does student need?
Manage investigation process?
Communication with wider community?

content.text: Scenario 4: Food Poisoning Outbreak. 15+ students are ill with vomiting/diarrhea after lunch. The symptoms suggest food poisoning. More are showing symptoms every hour. Parents are alarmed. Discussion:

items: Immediate actions for ill students?
Determine source; prevent spread?
Who investigate? What authority notify?
Communicate with parents?
Should the school close? For how long?
What happens with food service?
Manage reputation and parent confidence?

steps: Introduction (15 min): The facilitator explains; the scenario is presented; ground rules are set out
Initial Situation (30 min): Discuss immediate actions, priorities and roles
Injects (60 min): The facilitator adds complications; participants discuss how to respond
Recovery Phase (30 min): Discuss the medium and long term; business continuity; the return to normal
Debrief (30 min): What did we learn? What gaps did we find? What would we do differently? What are the action items?

content.text: Outbreak Response Plan:
Scenario: Several students/staff are ill with the same symptoms
Trigger for Activation: 5+ cases of same illness in 1 week

steps: Notification: Report to the local health department (Puskesmas/Dinas Kesehatan)
Tracking: Record all cases (names, symptoms, date symptoms started, classroom, contacts)
Enhanced Cleaning: Disinfect more often; focus on affected areas
Communication: Tell parents about the outbreak, the symptoms to watch for, and when to keep their child at home
Isolation: Ill students are isolated until a parent picks them up; staff with symptoms are sent home
Absence Policy: Flexible sick leave; encourage people to stay home; no penalties
Health Department Guidance: Follow its recommendations (these may include closures, screening, testing)
Consider School Closure: If a significant % are ill OR the health department recommends it
Reopening Criteria: Consult the health department; make sure the outbreak is contained; enhanced cleaning is completed

content.text: Full records and careful analysis build a stronger safety culture and lead to improvement.
Purpose: Classify incidents so that the response, reporting and analysis are appropriate.
Classification Levels:
Near-Miss: An event that could have caused injury/damage but did not

items: Examples: A student slips but stops their own fall. An object falls but no one is nearby. A fire alarm fault is found before it causes a false evacuation
Response: Document it; investigate contributing factors; put preventive measures in place

content.text: Minor Incident: Minor injury or property damage; no lasting impact

items: Examples: Small cut or scrape; bruise; minor illness (headache); small item broken
Response: First aid. Parent notification if there is an injury. Logged in EduNav where available, or in the approved interim incident log. No formal investigation unless there is a pattern

content.text: Significant Incident: Moderate injury that needs medical attention; notable property damage; disruption

items: Examples: Fracture, cut that needs stitches, serious allergic reaction; significant property damage; extended utility outage
Response: Medical treatment; parent communication; Principal notified; incident report completed; investigation if needed; risk register reviewed

content.text: Major Incident: Serious injury that needs a hospital stay; major property damage; significant disruption; possible breach of regulations

items: Examples: Head injury with loss of consciousness; severe burns; hospitalization; major structural damage; hazmat (hazardous materials) spill; serious safeguarding concern

Response: Emergency services called; full incident management activated; Principal takes command. GM/Foundation Representative notified; Yayasan informed. Full investigation; formal report; regulatory notification if required. Risk register updated; corrective actions carried out

content.text: Critical Incident: Death, permanent disability or catastrophic damage; major reputational, legal or regulatory consequences

items: Examples: Death, severe permanent injury; major fire or structural collapse; serious crime; major safeguarding failure

Response: Full crisis management; emergency services. Immediate notification to GM, Yayasan, Eduversal Central. External investigation (police, authorities); legal counsel engaged. Media management; full review; systemic changes carried out

content.text: First Responder Actions (any staff member who sees the incident or responds first):

steps: Ensure Safety: Make the scene safe; remove hazards or move people away from danger
Assess Severity: What happened? Is anyone injured? How serious is it?
Provide Aid: First aid for injuries; comfort for people in distress

items: Medical emergency: School nurse + ambulance if serious
Security threat: Security + Principal + police if needed
Property damage/hazard: Facilities staff

steps: Secure Scene: Preserve evidence if an investigation is needed
Notify Principal: Report the incident to the Principal or a senior leader immediately
Document: Write down what you saw, heard and did as soon as possible

content.text: Principal Actions (when notified of a significant or major incident):

steps: Assess: Get the facts: What happened? Who was involved? What is the current status?
Command: Take on the Incident Commander role if Level 3 or 4; delegate if Level 2
Resource: Deploy resources (ERT, external emergency services)
Communicate: Notify the GM/Foundation Representative; parents of the students involved; the Yayasan if major; Eduversal Central if major
Coordinate: Oversee the response; make decisions; adjust as the situation changes
Document: Make sure there is thorough documentation from the beginning

content.text: Section 6: Root Cause Analysis (for major incidents):
Use the "5 Whys" technique to find the underlying root cause:
Example:

items: Incident: Student fell from playground equipment and fractured arm
Why 1: Why did student fall? → Lost grip on monkey bars
Why 2: Why did the student lose grip? → Hands were wet from rain
Why 3: Why were hands wet? → Playground equipment used during rain
Why 4: Why was it used during rain? → Teacher didn't know the policy prohibits use when wet
Why 5: Why didn't the teacher know? → New staff were not trained on the playground safety policy
Root Cause: Inadequate induction training for new staff on playground safety
What must be done to stop it happening again?
Assign responsibility and deadlines
Example: "Revise staff induction checklist to include playground safety training; HR Manager; by [date]"

content.text: Permendikbud No. 33/2019 — Penyelenggaraan Program Satuan Pendidikan Aman Bencana (SPAB)

items: Requirements: disaster-risk assessment, preparedness, procedures, capacity building, coordination, and continuity measures appropriate to the school's hazard profile.

content.title: Risk Management to Support Insurability:

content.text: Risk management, emergency preparedness, and business continuity are essential responsibilities of school leadership. This section gives you frameworks, protocols, and procedures. They help you anticipate, prevent, and respond to threats to your school's mission: excellent education in a safe environment.

steps: Prevention is Best: finding and reducing risks early prevents incidents before they happen
Preparedness Saves Lives: training, drills, and planning make sure the response works when incidents do happen
Communication is Critical: clear communication with all stakeholders, on time, during and after emergencies keeps trust and safety
Learning is Continuous: Every incident, drill, and near-miss is an opportunity to improve
Documentation Demonstrates Accountability: good records show due diligence. They support accreditation, compliance, and legal requirements
Safety is Everyone's Responsibility: build a culture where all staff and students actively help with safety
content.title: Core Principles to Remember:

content.text: Your Role as Principal: You are the Incident Commander, the final decision-maker in emergencies, and the champion of safety culture. Your visible commitment to risk management sets the tone for the whole school community. You build risk management into daily operations and carry out regular reviews. You keep strong relationships with your GM/Foundation Representative and Yayasan, and you empower your Emergency Response Team. In this way you make sure your school is resilient and prepared. Your school can then continue its educational mission even when there is disruption.

items: Prioritize safety over convenience
Communicate early and often
Seek expert advice
Document everything
Learn from every experience
content.title: When in Doubt:

content.text: Your students, staff, and families trust you to keep them safe. This section gives you the knowledge and tools to honor that trust.

items: Review your current risk register and update as needed
Conduct or schedule your next emergency drill
Check that your emergency contact information is current
Confirm your Emergency Response Team members know their roles
Schedule your next risk review meeting with your GM/Foundation Representative
